summary.text: At source level, RequestPublisher.ExecuteAsync creates one Kafka producer using KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP or kafka:9092, with idempotence enabled and a 10-second message timeout. While the token is not cancelled, it calls PublishPending and waits one second between passes. PublishPending selects at most one eligible unpublished row in created_at order with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; if none is returned, it exits that pass without sending. For a selected row it extracts place.id from the stored JSON, awaits a send to weather.place-requested using that ID as the key, then sets published=true and commits the database transaction. Since send completion comes before the database commit, a crash between them can leave the row eligible for another send. The loop logs other exceptions as PUBLISH_RETRY; cancellation during PublishPending breaks the loop, while cancellation reaching the post-attempt delay can propagate. C# source coverage is PARTIAL; this code does not establish runtime hosting activation or delivery.

operations.title: Place request publisher

summary.text: ExecuteAsync creates a producer and repeatedly calls PublishPending until cancellation, logging other exceptions as PUBLISH_RETRY and waiting one second between attempts. Each publish opens a database transaction and selects one eligible unpublished row in created_at order with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; no row returns without sending. Otherwise it extracts the place ID from the payload, awaits a keyed send to weather.place-requested, marks the row published, and commits. A broker send followed by a transaction failure or crash can leave the row eligible for replay. The Dashboard and Forecasts topic mappings are agent-proposed; subscription, downstream processing and hosted-service activation remain unverified.
